items.title: Not All Longing Is Craving: The Aspiration to Liberation Itself Falls Outside the Chain

items.zh: 問：若受為緣，皆是愛耶？設是愛者，皆受為緣耶？答：應作四句：或有是愛非受為緣，謂希求勝解脫，及依善愛而捨餘愛。或受為緣而非是愛，謂除無明觸所生受為緣，所餘有支法生。或有受為緣亦是愛，謂無明觸所生受為緣，染污愛生。
items.en: Question: If a thing is conditioned by feeling, is it necessarily craving? And if it is craving, is it necessarily conditioned by feeling? Answer: Four cases should be made. There is craving not conditioned by feeling — the aspiration to supreme liberation, and the wholesome longing by which every other, lesser longing is renounced. There is what is conditioned by feeling yet is not craving — every remaining link that arises with feeling born of ignorance-conditioned contact as its condition, craving excepted. There is what is both conditioned by feeling and is craving — craving tainted by feeling arisen from ignorance-conditioned contact.

items.zh: 除如是相，是第四句。問：若愛為緣，皆是取耶？設是取者，皆愛為緣耶？答：當知此中是順後句。謂所有取皆愛為緣。或愛為緣而非是取。謂除取所餘有支，及緣善愛、勤精進等諸善法生。問：若取為緣，皆是有耶？設是有者，皆取為緣耶？答：亦應作順後句。謂所有有皆取為緣。或取為緣而非是有。謂除有，所餘有支。問：若有為緣，皆是生耶？設是生者，皆有為緣耶？答：諸所有生皆有為緣。或有為緣而非是生。謂除生，所餘老死最後有支。問：若生為緣，皆老死耶？設是老死，皆生為緣耶？答：所有老死皆生為緣。或生為緣而非老死。所謂疾病、怨憎合會、親愛別離、所求不遂、及彼所起愁歎憂苦種種熱惱。

items.title: Which Links Obstruct Which Parts of the Path, and Which Are Always Defiled

items.zh: 問：是諸有支，幾與道支所攝正見為勝障礙？答：無明，及彼所起意行，若有一分能為勝障。如於正見，如是於正思惟及正精進亦爾。若正語、正業、正命，以身行、語行及有一分為勝障礙。若正命、正定，以餘有支為勝障礙應知。
items.en: Question: Of these links, which most strongly obstruct right view, one factor of the noble path? Answer: Ignorance, together with the mental formation it gives rise to, and a portion of becoming, are its strongest obstruction. Right thought and right effort should be understood the same way. Right speech, right action, and right livelihood are most strongly obstructed by bodily and verbal formation, and by a portion of becoming. Right mindfulness and right concentration should be understood as most strongly obstructed by the remaining links.

items.zh: 問：是諸有支，幾唯雜染品？幾通雜染、清淨品？答：四唯雜染品，餘通雜染、清淨品。問：云何生支通二品耶？答：若生惡趣及有難處，唯是雜染品；若生人天諸無難處，此通染淨品。當知餘支，隨其所應皆通二品。
items.en: Question: Of these links, how many belong to defilement alone? How many can belong to either defilement or purity? Answer: Four belong to defilement alone; the rest can belong to either. Question: How can the link of birth belong to either? Answer: Birth into an unfortunate destiny, or into any circumstance of genuine hardship, belongs to defilement alone; birth among ordinary humans or gods, free of such hardship, can belong to either.

items.title: Three Grades of Ignorance Whose Cessation Actually Stops Formations

items.zh: 問：何等無明不有故行不有，何等無明滅故行滅耶？答：有三種，發起、纏、隨眠無明，由此無明滅故，彼無明滅；由彼滅故，行亦隨滅。
items.en: Question: Which ignorance not existing means formations do not exist? Which ignorance ceasing means formations cease? Answer: There are three — the ignorance that initiates a deed, ignorance as active manifestation, and ignorance as dormant latent tendency. Because this dormant ignorance ceases, manifest ignorance ceases; and because that ceases, formations cease as well, following in turn.

items.zh: 問：何等行不有故識不有，何等行滅故識滅耶？答：諸行於自相續中已作已滅，及未起對治，又由意行有故，起身語行；由此有故彼有。彼無故，彼緣識亦無；此若全滅，當知識亦隨滅。
items.en: Question: Which formations not existing means consciousness does not exist? Which formations ceasing means consciousness ceases? Answer: Formations already performed and already passed within one's own continuing stream, not yet met by any genuine antidote, together with mental formation giving rise to bodily and verbal formation in turn — it is by these existing that consciousness, conditioned by them, exists. Where these do not exist, consciousness conditioned by them does not exist either; and where they are entirely extinguished, consciousness, it should be understood, ceases along with them.

items.zh: 問：何等識不有故名色不有，何等識滅故名色滅耶？答：種子識不有故，果識不有。此俱滅故，俱名色滅。如識望名色道理，如是餘支乃至受，隨其所應，當知亦爾。如無明緣行道理，如是愛緣取、取緣有道理，當知亦爾。如行緣識道理，如是有緣生，當知亦爾。如識緣名色道理，生緣老死，當知亦爾。問：何等受不有故愛不有，何等受滅故愛滅耶？答：如行緣識道理，當知亦爾。問：

items.title: Three Topics Close in Sequence: Cessation Finishes, the Twelve Links Located Among Eight Gateways, and Five Faults Against Five Benefits

items.zh: 如前所說八緣起門，幾門是十二支緣起所顯，幾門非耶？答：三門是彼所顯，謂二一分所顯，一全分所顯；餘門非。何等為二一分所顯？謂內識生門、自業所作門。何等為一全分所顯？謂有情世間轉門。
items.en: Of the eight gateways of dependent origination named earlier, how many are displayed by the twelve links, and how many are not? Answer: Three are so displayed — two only in part, one in full; the rest are not. Which two are displayed only in part? The gateway of an inward consciousness arising, and the gateway of one's own accumulated karma's dominant power. Which one is displayed in full? The gateway of a sentient being's death and birth.

items.zh: 問：不如實知緣起道理者，有幾種過患耶？答：有五。謂起我見，及能發起前際俱行見。如前際俱行見，如是後際俱行見、前後際俱行見亦爾。又於彼見猛利堅執，有取有怖，於現法中不般涅槃，是名第五過患。問：如實知者，有幾種勝利耶？答：翻前五過，應知勝利亦有五種。復次，
items.en: Question: How many faults follow for one who does not truly know the nature of dependent origination? Answer: Five. Self-view arises; a view bound up with the past arises together with it; a view bound up with the future arises the same way; and a view bound up with the juncture of past and future, the present, arises the same way; and fiercely, firmly clinging to these views — grasping them, and dreading nirvāṇa — one fails to reach nirvāṇa in this very life: this is the fifth fault. Question: How many benefits follow for one who does truly know it? Answer: The reverse of these same five faults — five benefits should be understood accordingly.

blocks.text: Today's reading begins with a reassurance many practitioners need: the longing for liberation is not the craving that drives saṃsāra. It then shows which links obstruct which parts of the path, which are always defiled, and what goes wrong for one who does not understand dependent origination.

"Not all longing is craving." The longing for liberation is a love "not conditioned by feeling". Master Cháng Bǎi: "This uncontaminated wholesome love can destroy the three existences, so it is not the craving link; though it is love, it is not craving." (Ru-Yi's reading note says the treatise never calls it craving; in fact the Chinese does use 愛 for it, but explicitly places it outside the chain.)

This answers a common worry: "If craving is the problem, isn't wanting enlightenment just more craving?" The treatise distinguishes them by their source and effect. Craving arises from feeling and moistens rebirth; aspiration to liberation arises from understanding and dries it up.

"Ignorance, together with the mental formation it gives rise to, and a portion of becoming" most strongly obstruct right view. Other links obstruct right intention and the rest. For right mindfulness and concentration, Venerable Miào Jìng: "the worst are craving and grasping; when they are active and you want concentration …" Every meditator knows the end of that sentence.

Some links are always defiled; others can be either. Birth into an unfortunate destiny or into hardship is defiled; birth among humans or gods free of hardship "can be either", because such a birth can support the path. (The text says "four" are purely defiled; Venerable Miào Jìng notes that the *Pīxún jì* suspects "three", and Kuījī adds consciousness to make four.)

Ignorance is of three kinds: initiating (that drives action), manifest (active now), and latent (as seed). Venerable Miào Jìng: "When latent ignorance ceases, manifest ignorance is gone; with both gone, initiating ignorance is gone too." And: calm alone cannot cut the latent; insight is needed.

Of the eight gateways of Day 66, the twelve links display three: inner consciousness and one's own karma in part, beings' death and rebirth in full. Master Cháng Bǎi: the links cover consciousness only as one link, so they do not exhaust it.

Not truly knowing dependent origination brings five faults: self-view; views bound up with the past, the future, and the present (Venerable Miào Jìng: "prior and posterior" again means the present); and fierce clinging to these views with dread. Master Cháng Bǎi: "One dreads nirvāṇa, and so does not reach it in this life." Knowing dependent origination brings the five opposite benefits. This is the practical reason for all the analysis of the last four days: understanding how saṃsāra works removes the fear of its ending.

quiz.q: §22 says longing for liberation "is craving not conditioned by feeling." The reading note says it's "never called craving." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: the text does call it 愛, but this wholesome love destroys existence and isn't the craving link — so the note is inaccurate
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "This uncontaminated wholesome love can destroy the three existences, so it's not the craving link — though it is love, it isn't the love among afflictions." The text says "there is craving not conditioned by feeling — the aspiration to supreme liberation." So the note's "never called craving" is inaccurate.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, which links most strongly obstruct right view?
options: ignorance, the mental formation it produces, and a portion of becoming
quiz.why: "Ignorance, together with the mental formation it gives rise to, and a portion of becoming, are its strongest obstruction." The same holds for right thought and effort; right speech, action, and livelihood are blocked by bodily and verbal formation. Venerable Miào Jìng: 若 here means "and," and 有 is the becoming link.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, how can the link of birth belong to both defilement and purity?
options: birth in unfortunate destinies or hardship is purely defiled; birth among humans or gods free of hardship can be either
quiz.why: "Birth into an unfortunate destiny, or into any circumstance of genuine hardship, belongs to defilement alone; birth among ordinary humans or gods, free of such hardship, can belong to either." Venerable Miào Jìng on the eight hardships: even Uttarakuru counts — no one there bothers to learn the Dharma.

quiz.q: Right mindfulness and concentration are obstructed by "the remaining links." Which matter most, according to the teachers?
options: craving and grasping — when they're active, concentration is hard
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The worst are craving and grasping — when they're active and you want concentration …" Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the *Yuqie lunji*: "In principle, only craving and grasping should be said to obstruct right mindfulness and concentration."

quiz.q: The text names three ignorances: initiating, manifest, and latent. In what order do they cease, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: when latent ignorance ceases, manifest ignorance goes; with both gone, initiating ignorance goes — and calm alone can't cut the latent, one must penetrate reality
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "When latent ignorance ceases, manifest ignorance is gone; with both gone, initiating ignorance is gone too," and citing the *Xianyang*: "only by penetrating the true nature of things are afflictions' seeds cut." The text: "Because this dormant ignorance ceases, manifest ignorance ceases; and … formations cease."

quiz.q: Of the eight gateways named earlier, how many are displayed by the twelve links?
options: three — inward consciousness and one's own karma in part; beings' death and birth in full
quiz.why: "Three are so displayed — two only in part, one in full; the rest are not." The two in part: inward consciousness arising, and one's own karma; in full: beings' death and birth. Master Cháng Bǎi: the purification gateway belongs to reversal and isn't displayed by the twelve links.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, how many faults follow from not truly knowing dependent origination?
options: five: self-view; views tied to the past, the future, and both; and fierce clinging with grasping and dread, failing to reach nirvāṇa in this life
quiz.why: "Five. Self-view arises; a view bound up with the past arises together with it; … and fiercely, firmly clinging to these views — grasping them, and dreading … — one fails to reach nirvāṇa in this very life." The reverse gives five benefits. Venerable Miào Jìng: the fifth is clinging to views; the three-time views are extreme views.
